title: An empty command-level run: is refused by all with a pointer to a bare command that cannot run
body:
## Problem

An empty command-level `run:` is refused twice and one of the two refusals points somewhere false. `cfg_validate` already refuses it by key (`lib/config:778`), but only `doctor` and `release` run validation. On the dispatch path, `<command> all` over a command-level `run:` is refused by `run_all` (`lib/resolve:1017`) with "'bin/devbin <command>' runs it", and the bare command then refuses the empty line itself through `run_words` and `warn_no_words` (`lib/helpers:319`, `:396`). Both exit 1, so there is no false green; the pointer to a command that cannot run is the defect. Parked at the 0.1.8 cut; fixed forward in the bundle on hv's word, 2026-10-03.

## Measured at 2ce9411 (0152 v1 on 953d040; cc's evidence pass)

With `commands.probe.run: ""`: `probe` prints "commands.probe.run holds no words, so there is no command to run", rc 1; `probe all` prints "'bin/devbin probe all' has no options to run: commands.probe.run in bin/.devbin/config.yaml owns probe here, and 'bin/devbin probe' runs it", then "0 of 0 probe options ran...", rc 1. A whitespace-only `run:` behaves the same. No shipped or reference config declares an empty `run:`.

## Fix

In `run_all`'s run-tier branch, ask `has_words` of the declared line, and when it holds none, refuse with `warn_no_words "commands.<command>.run"` -- the bare command's own words -- in place of the pointer. The exit status and the count line stay.

## Done when

1. `<command> all` over an empty or blank `run:` names the key and says it holds no words, and no longer says the bare command runs it; red at 2ce9411.
2. A `run:` with words keeps today's pointer.

## Resolution

Fixed at 98d4b646. In run_all's run-tier refusal the declared command-level `run:` is asked `has_words`, read through cfg_get as the bare command reads it. With no words, `<command> all` refuses with the bare command's own sentence, that `commands.<command>.run` holds no words, and no longer says the bare command runs it; with words it keeps the pointer. The exit status and the count line are unchanged.

Against the done-when list:

1. An empty and a blank `run:` each name the key and say it holds no words, and never "runs it": dispatch.bats's (0160) arm, red on the code beneath this change, which printed the pointer.
2. A `run:` with words keeps today's pointer: the same arm's last case.

Evidence. 2 mutants, both killed. The arms run green under GNU coreutils, findutils and sed as well as the BSD tools. The full suite on the landing tree: vc's full suite, on main af758c10 (code at 415ce738) with 0163 v3.1 and 0167 git-am'd and cc's 0155, 0160, 0161 and 0162 applied above them, in a fresh clone: 2190 of 2190 ok, 0 not ok, its .errors empty (seal 20261006-0607), 06:07:26Z to 06:55:27Z; 5 skipped, the expected five: two arms that need a runner with no controlling terminal, two require_command arms whose expected outcome is a skip, and a case-folding disk.
